title: Wendell and the Orchard
premise: Ivo Vasquez, a ghostwriter who believes the heart can be trained like any muscle, takes an anonymous pen-pal assignment meant to pair strangers — only to discover her assigned correspondent is Wendell Marsh, the rival memoirist whose book she is secretly writing and the man she blames for her family bakery's collapse. Their letters, written without names, strip away the armor of their public feud, while in person they spar over a shared orchard property that could save or doom her expiring lease. When both identities are exposed at once, Ivo must choose between finishing the memoir that will bury him and confessing that the person she most needs to forgive is herself, for walking away from the orchard years ago. She signs the lease, publishes under her own name at last, and meets Wendell beneath the apple trees as two people finally unmasked.
about_author: B. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper columnist who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming one of her own. She lives near an abandoned orchard whose last surviving tree inspired this novel.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ghostwriting a rival's memoir by day, Ivo lectures her sister that love is trainable, containable — then receives an anonymous pen-pal assignment from her writers' guild. Beat: confident control established, first hairline crack.

chapters.title: Letter One
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell, stung by a scathing review, joins the pen-pal program on a dare from his editor. His first letter is deliberately prickly; the reply he gets back is pricklier. Beat: antagonism disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Terms of the Lease
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The bakery lease on her late mother's storefront expires in ninety days unless she can secure the adjoining orchard parcel its landlord is selling. The competing bidder: Wendell Marsh. Beat: stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Correspondence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV via letters. Anonymous, they argue about memory, forgiveness, and whether people can change — each unknowingly describing the other. Beat: intimacy growing inside hostility.

chapters.title: The Orchard Walk
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo surveys the orchard and runs into Wendell; their public sparring masks how closely his words echo her pen pal's. She notices he flinches at the old well. Beat: first dissonance between enemy and letter-writer.

chapters.title: What Mother Left
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sorting her mother's things, Ivo finds a ledger revealing her mother once borrowed against the orchard to keep the bakery alive — and that Wendell's father held the debt. Beat: guilt resurfaces; identity theme deepens.

chapters.title: Deadlines
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell's memoir deadline looms and his ghostwriter's draft feels hollow. He writes his pen pal something honest for the first time. Beat: vulnerability leaks through the mask.

chapters.title: Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The orchard goes to sealed-bid auction. Ivo's savings fall short; her sister urges her to walk away, echoing the voice in Ivo's own head. Beat: despair hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Well
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell visits the orchard at dusk and finds Ivo there. Trapped by rain in the packing shed, they talk without armor for ten minutes before retreating. Beat: almost-tender moment, immediately denied.

chapters.title: Confession in Ink
chapters.summary: Letters, alternating. Her pen pal admits a failure that destroyed someone's livelihood; hers admits she left home and never came back until it was too late. Beat: mutual confession, dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Rival's Draft
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Reading Wendell's raw memoir chapters, Ivo recognizes the boy in them — the one who was blamed for the fire that closed the bakery district. Her ghostwritten framing has been wrong. Beat: moral crisis begins.

chapters.title: Bids and Betrayals
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell wins the auction but discovers his publisher engineered it as publicity for the memoir — using Ivo's bakery story as the hook. Beat: rage; the machinery of duty revealed.

chapters.title: Unmasked
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At a public reading, the publisher reveals both secrets at once: Ivo is the ghostwriter, and their pen-pal letters are read aloud as 'research.' Beat: climax of humiliation; identity shattered publicly.

chapters.title: The Mirror
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo rereads her own letters and sees the cruelty she aimed at a stranger who turned out to be a wounded boy she never questioned. She confronts her reflection. Beat: the forgiveness theme turns inward.

chapters.title: What the Fire Was
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell finally tells the truth about the fire — his father's negligence, not his — and why he bought the orchard: to give it back. Beat: truth as release.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With three days left on the lease, Ivo refuses Wendell's gift and instead negotiates: she'll buy half the orchard with money earned publishing her own book — if he'll let her rewrite the memoir honestly, credited to neither of them alone. Beat: love choosing terms over surrender.

chapters.title: Signing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They sign co-ownership papers in the bakery, flour on their hands, arguing about apple varieties like an old married couple. Beat: warmth earned through friction.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Letters, alternating. Each writes one final anonymous letter — a goodbye to the person they were — and mails them to themselves. Beat: elegy and gratitude braided together.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The rewritten memoir releases under both their names; Ivo's own book about her mother follows. Reviewers call it ruthless and tender. Beat: identity claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Winter work in the orchard; quiet domesticity tested when Ivo gets an offer to ghostwrite in Paris again. She asks what he'd do. He says stay, and means it without conditions. Beat: love against duty, resolved gently.

chapters.title: First Bloom
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Spring: the old trees blossom for the first time in years. Ivo forgives her mother aloud at the well, Wendell beside her. Beat: emotional resolution of the memory theme.

chapters.title: Wendell and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing frame. A year later, they teach a pen-pal workshop where strangers write to strangers; Ivo reads her first letter aloud, laughing at who she used to be. Under the blossoms, Wendell asks her to stay for good. Beat: full-circle joy; the heart, trained at last, chooses freely.
